ledger.note: 1325: Prolaya Vema Reddi founds the Reddi kingdom at Addanki. 'It was established by Prolaya Vema Reddy in 1325' ('in about 1325', Prolaya Vema Reddy page); the Kakatiya empire 'came to an end in 1323' and the Tughlaqs held the region only briefly. The page gives no boundary.

1328: the capital moves from Addanki to the fortified Kondavidu. 'Later, it was moved to the fortified Kondavidu to safeguard the kingdom' against 'the regular invasions of Recherla Velama rulers and their Bahamani allies' (Reddy page, undated). The Kondavidu Fort page dates the move: 'It was used as the capital by the Reddy dynasty between 1328 and 1482, shifting from their former capital at Addanki' and 'He shifted his capital from Addanki in Guntur to Kondaveedu fort' under Prolaya Vema Reddy (r. 1325-1353), '(1328-1428)' for the dynasty there; the Prolaya Vema Reddy page instead has his successor Anavota Reddi (after 1353) establishing the capital at Kondavidu. The two pages disagree on the king; 1328 is the Kondavidu Fort page's year. [Repair 2026-10-20: confidence 1 to 2.]

region.text: Rajahmundry and its country, short of Telangana

ledger.note: 1395: a Reddi branch is set up at Rajahmundry. 'Another subsidiary branch of the Reddi Kingdom was established in 1395 at Rajahmundry'; the page does not say whom the country was taken from. The coast between the Krishna and the Godavari was Musunuri land until 1368 (Musunuri page) and goes to nobody in the musunuri-nayaks ledger, which is why this gain names 'nobody'.

ledger.note: 1424: Vijayanagara annexes Kondavidu. 'In 1424, Kondavidu was annexed by the Vijayanagara Empire.' The Deva Raya II page dates a battle of Kondavidu to c. 1427 against Bhanudeva IV and says 'An invasion by the Reddis of Kondavidu was also repulsed' (undated).
1424: the surviving Reddis rule from Rajahmundry. The page puts the Rajahmundry branch's conquest by the Gajapatis 'some 25 years' after the loss of Kondavidu; the seat is a reading.

1448: the Gajapatis take Rajahmundry and end the Reddi kingdom. 'The kingdom of Rajahmundry was thus brought under the sway of Kapilendra before A. D. 1448' (Kapilendra Deva page); 'The Reddy Kingdom... existed from 1325 to 1448 CE' (Reddy page: 'Rajahmundry was conquered by the Gajapatis some 25 years later' than 1424).

notes:
No Cliopatria row. Pages: Reddy Kingdom, Prolaya Vema Reddy (same content), Kondavidu Fort, Deva Raya II, Musunuri Nayaks, plus Kapilendra Deva for 1448. The pages give no area, no ruler list that can be matched to names (the infobox reign ranges 1325-1353, 1353-1364, 1364-1386, 1386-1402, 1395-1414, 1402-1420, 1420-1424, 1414-1423, 1423-1448 have no names in the text), no capital dates and no wars with dates, so the dossier is thin; rulers omitted.
Disagreements: Kondavidu to Vijayanagara in 1424 (Reddy page) against a battle of Kondavidu c. 1427 with Bhanudeva IV (Deva Raya II page); the Kondavidu Fort page dates the Reddys 1328-1428 and 'between 1328 and 1482'; the Reddy page says the dynasty 'remained in power until the mid 15th century' (the Rajahmundry branch).
Not settled: the extent 'from Cuttack to Kanchi and Srisailam' (undated, not drawn); Anavota Reddi's and Anavema Reddy's conquests (their pages do not exist under those titles); the move to Kondavidu; where the Rajahmundry land came from in 1395.
Counterparts needing a dossier: recherla-velamas (Telangana, to 1435; the Musunuri page says they annexed the Musunuri lands in 1368), musunuri-nayaks (1333-1368, Warangal).

[Repair 2026-10-20, sa-04-x-fix] Region: the drawn Reddi shape no longer crosses the Krishna (see the first keyframe). Capital move to Kondavidu raised from confidence 1 to 2 on the Kondavidu Fort page's 1328 (the Prolaya Vema Reddy page credits Anavota Reddi instead). Ruler strip added from the Kondavidu Fort page (Prolaya Vema Reddy, r. 1325-1353) and the Prolaya page (Anavota Reddi as successor; years a reading of the infobox ranges). Still thin: the maximum extent (Cuttack, Kanchi, Srisailam) is undated on the Reddy page and is not drawn; the Reddy page has no names for the nine infobox reigns. Gazetteer names needed: 'Krishna-Godavari doab' (coastal Andhra between the two rivers) so the 12-point divider can be replaced by a named region; Addanki and Kondavidu.
